name: Triple Divide
generated_description:
Triple Divide is a 2,523-foot summit in Pennsylvania. The Triple Divide Trail covers 2.5 miles with about 768 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

The climbing is spread fairly evenly from start to finish rather than stacked into one steep section. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 1.07, gaining roughly 1,200 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 1,732 feet, the route tops out near 2,500 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 41.81289, -77.788 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 150 miles northeast of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Moderate rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include White Knoll, Big Level and Mount Brodhead — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: It's rated Moderate using the National Park Service difficulty formula (2.5 miles, 768 ft of gain — about 300 ft of climbing per mile). The elevation profile on this page shows exactly where the steep sections fall.

faqs.question: Where is the Triple Divide trailhead?
faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 41.81289, -77.788 in Pennsylvania. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the Triple Divide trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Triple Divide?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Triple Divide?
faqs.answer: Triple Divide stands at 2,523 feet (769 meters) in Pennsylvania.
